Lo, Iron and stone, my hands have wrought fair work,
Nigh this great bridge where verdant floods and whitened willows part.
But now the thaw does pluck at this brittle frost,
A plan of sapphire girdles long awoke
Does now give way, laid low in winter’s hag.
Though to build with hot iron in winter's grip
Is folly fraught, yet to forsake,
What we have dared to build, makes my heart chill.
So, let me bind the leaking joints with stanching mortar,
And lay up hope for spring in the stones of the span.
For though we cannot yet work with blazes of fires,
The stones shall hold whilst winter’s heart may chill.
